title: the greeting that is a wish
hookLine: the greeting that is a wish; s-l-m — salaam, Muslim, Islam
last: EID — JOY THAT COMES BACK AROUND.

cards: In a shop, at an airport gate, across a dinner table: two people meet, and before how are you, before the weather, one says as-salamu alaykum. The other answers straight back: wa alaykum as-salam.
It happens so fast it sounds like hello. It isn't hello. Hello says I see you.
This greeting hands the other person something. And the word at its center is hiding inside the name of the faith itself.

teach.b: Salaam means peace. As-salamu alaykum: peace be upon you. A wish, given in the first second of meeting someone.
Here's the part that surprises people. Arabic builds its words from roots, usually three letters. This one is s, l, m.
Put different vowels around it and you get salaam: peace. You get Islam: the surrender, the making of peace with God. And you get Muslim: a person who does that.
So every time two Muslims greet each other, they say a piece of the faith's own name. The Qur'an even gives the word to God: among God's names is As-Salam, Peace itself.

teach.h: ANSWER WITH BETTER, OR THE SAME.
teach.b: And it sets a rule for answering: “When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it.” The minimum is to give the peace back.
Better is to add to it: and upon you peace, and the mercy of God, and His blessings. The greeting grows as it goes around.
A saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ties it to love: you won't truly love one another, he told his companions, until you spread salaam among yourselves.

teach.h: THE GREETING FIRST, THEN THE LOVE.
teach.b: Not a feeling first and then a greeting. The greeting first, and the love grows from it.

how: Muslims greet one another with "as-salamu alaykum" (peace be upon you) and answer "wa alaykum as-salam" (and upon you peace), often adding "and the mercy of God and His blessings." The greeting is also said to close each daily prayer.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: the root of salaam, Islam, Muslim
Peace: a name of God in the Qur'an

s: it means peace be upon you. it's a wish, handed over in the first second.
salaam, Islam and Muslim share one Arabic root
s-l-m. peace, the surrender that makes peace, and the person who does it.
the Qur'an says to answer a greeting with a better one, or the same
surah 4, verse 86: "greet ye with a better than it or return it."

games.q: someone says to you: as-salamu alaykum. by the Qur'an's rule, what's the best answer?
o: give it back, or give back more.
say it first next time instead.
games.why: "greet ye with a better than it or return it" (4:86). the minimum is to return the peace. better is to add mercy and blessings.

practice: Sit comfortably and let your breathing slow. Bring to mind one person you'll see today. Breathe in, and on the way out send them the word, silently: salaam, peace upon you.
Then someone harder to greet. The same word, the same breath. Stay with it.

wordCard.voice: Salaam. Peace: the greeting that's a gift, and the root inside Islam and Muslim. Eighth word.

orig.note: Arabic. peace. the root s-l-m also gives Islam (إسلام) and Muslim (مسلم).

carryVoice: Your line: peace, upon you. The Qur'an's rule for answering: with better, or at least the same. Day eight.

sources.q: When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it.
